visual_goal: Show one control plane beneath every product: the tenant directory defines the customer, Axleby ID decides who may act, Baseline configures, Charter governs data use, and Meterline turns usage into invoices.
prompt: A layered illustration. Top: a wide band of four product tiles side by side, labeled 'Lotwise', 'Showroomly', 'Data APIs' and 'Trade'. Below it, a foundation layer of three boxes left to right: a person badge with a key labeled 'Axleby ID', a slider panel labeled 'Baseline', and a scroll with a seal labeled 'Charter'. One upward arrow from 'Axleby ID' into the product band labeled 'who may act'. One upward arrow from 'Baseline' into the product band labeled 'how it behaves'. One upward arrow from 'Charter' into the product band labeled 'what data may be used for'. At the very bottom, a wide base block shaped like an organization tree labeled 'Tenant directory', with one arrow up into 'Axleby ID' and one arrow up into 'Baseline'. To the right of the product band, one arrow out to a meter dial labeled 'Meterline', labeled 'usage events', and one arrow from 'Meterline' down to a stack of plain invoice sheets with only lines and a euro sign '€', labeled 'Invoices'. These ten labels plus the four arrow labels are the only words in the image. The product band has no header or title above it; each tile shows only its own label and a simple plain icon with no currency symbols.
alt: A tenant directory base supports Axleby ID and Baseline; with Charter they feed the product band of Lotwise, Showroomly, Data APIs and Trade; usage events flow to Meterline and on to invoices.
